conventions.convention: Countable Choice is assumed; no empirical premises or empirical-validity conclusions are asserted.
The physical cell is the three-dimensional torus of period 2πL. Dimensions one and two describe fields independent of omitted coordinates with zero omitted velocity components.
Normalized coordinates are x=X/L and τ=tU*/L; velocity and pressure scales are U* and ρ*U*². Fourier measure is (2π)^(-d)dx, and incompressible pressure has zero spatial mean.
The fixed polytropic pressure law is p=κ_phys ρ^γ with κ_phys>0 and γ>1; specific internal energy κ_phys ρ^(γ−1)/(γ−1) is an additional adopted closure. Density remains strictly positive.

Global evolution means smoothness and finite Sobolev norms on every compact forward time interval, without a uniform-in-time bound. The global theorem requires strictly positive viscosity and the two-dimensional invariant sector.

load_bearing.statement: Assuming Countable Choice, the stated force-free periodic polytropic model with fixed positive coefficient, exponent γ>1, and smooth positive-density data in dimensions one through three has unique smooth local evolution, remains positive, has bounded higher Sobolev norms on the same interval, and conserves the stated mean model energy.

Assuming Countable Choice, smooth real divergence-free periodic data in dimensions one through three and constant nonnegative viscosity give unique smooth local normalized velocity and mean-zero pressure. For integer s≥4, the lifespan depends only on d, s, and the initial H^s norm, independently of viscosity and higher initial norms; all higher Sobolev orders remain bounded there.

Assuming Countable Choice, every smooth real divergence-free datum for the stated force-free two-dimensional periodic incompressible model with constant positive density and viscosity has unique global smooth velocity and zero-mean pressure, also giving the stated transversely invariant three-dimensional mechanical evolution.

published_dependencies.used_for: Exact countable-choice assumption carried by all four assigned items and their mathematical evolution suppliers. The definition selects one member from each nonempty set in a family indexed by the natural numbers.
